data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment
* code_version: HEAD includes PR 332 post-recovery-fixes (added merge-commit support to git revert step)
* surfaced_by: live dryrun-bridge-rollback-in-worktree.sh against cutover SHA 12fa5560d8 (PR 327 merge)
* parent_story: 7339-ce88-39ff-4d31 (cutover + rollback dry-run)

### 2. Incident Overview
* Scenario Type: User-Flagged Behavior (surfaced during 7339 verifier re-audit per bug 75d4)

#### Expected Behavior
Rollback dryrun executes cleanly: revert cutover, restore cursor snapshot, commit, watch CI.

#### Actual Behavior
STEP 1 (revert) succeeds after the merge-commit fix.
STEP 2 (cursor restore) succeeds.
STEP 3 (commit) fails: Check tickets boundary hook rejects the rollback commit because reverting the cutover commit ALSO reverted the allowlist entry that exempted the fsck script from the boundary check. The fsck script (which existed before the cutover) still contains the same tracker-access lines, now without its allowlist entry.

Root cause: rollback scope mismatch. The cutover commit's blast radius is wider than just the cutover (it bundled the bands code + the allowlist update + the cutover). Reverting un-does adjacent infrastructure.

Recommended fix: rollback script detects allowlist-affected files in the diff and re-adds the relevant allowlist line for the duration of the rollback commit. Or accept --no-verify on the rollback commit as an emergency-operation tradeoff documented inline.

### 6. Logs
Full dryrun output saved at /tmp/7339-dryrun-output.txt during the 7339 verifier re-audit.
data.title: [rollback-bridge-cutover]: STEP 3 commit fails when revert drops allowlist entry for fsck script -> dryrun cannot complete cleanly
